subject: SIG follow-up: deployment boundaries and evidence for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: SIG - clarifications on deployment model questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. We've attached the SIG questionnaire and highlighted ~25 questions we need clarifications on related to deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC/on-prem). Two quick asks: 1) for each deployment mode, please indicate which controls are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed, and 2) point us to any diagrams or evidence for network boundaries and key management.

We're hoping to get a customer-ready answer set by EOD Monday (the 15th) for our internal reviewers.

Attached: SIG-Acme-questions.xlsx

Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of InfoSec, Acme Health

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG - clarifications on deployment model questions

Jordan — thanks for the note and the callout. We're on it. Quick summary of approach so you know what to expect:

- We'll produce a deployment-boundary matrix that maps each SIG question to the responsible party (Redwood vs Customer) for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC / on-prem).
- We'll attach a short evidence pack (network diagrams, KMS scope, audit-log retention statements) and a clear recommendation for the items that require customer configuration.
- Monica (CS) will collect any customer-specific configs needed for Dedicated/Private, Grace will own security wording and evidence, and Hannah will review any contract/pooled-risk language.

I'll circulate a draft by Friday EOD PST and target an internal review over the weekend so we can send a final version next Monday. If that timeline doesn't match your reviewers' needs let me know.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

---
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 16:27:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: SIG - clarifications on deployment model questions (draft answers attached)

Team — forwarding Acme's email and our working draft (attached). Key items where we need explicit language or evidence:

1) Customer data residency & control: For Hosted we must state that customer data is stored in the region selected and that Redwood encrypts data at rest using customer-zone keys for Enterprise customers; for Dedicated & Private, customer controls the VPC and key material.

2) KMS/Key ownership: Need final wording explaining HSM-backed KMS for Hosted enterprise customers vs customer-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private. Grace, can you confirm the exact phrasing we use in SOC 2 evidence?

3) Network boundary diagrams: I've created two diagrams (attached) — one showing Hosted flow with prefix/KV cache in Redwood-managed subnet and one for Dedicated where the GPU fleet is in a customer VPC peered to Redwood "control plane". Hannah — any legal redlines we should avoid when we describe "control plane" responsibilities?

4) Audit logs & access: For Hosted we should reference our audit-log retention (90 days default, enterprise options) and mention token-level tracing in Console. For Dedicated/Private, logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM; please confirm retention options.

Please add comments directly on the attached spreadsheet. I'll reconcile and produce the final merged answers Monday morning.

Thanks — K

Attachments: SIG-Acme-answers-draft-v1.xlsx; deployment-boundary-matrix-20260213.pdf; network-diagrams-hosted-dedicated-private.pdf

---
From: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmehealth.com, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG - clarifications on deployment model questions

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A couple of clarifications from our side before we finalize:

- For Hosted (multi-tenant), your sheet says "customer data encrypted at rest with keys in our KMS" — can you confirm if keys are tenant-specific or if you use envelope encryption with a single root? We need to know whether Acme can supply keys or use an enterprise KMS integration.

- For Dedicated, we need explicit language about whether the control plane can access the GPU subnet or if control plane actions are done via an agent with mutual TLS.

- For Private/on-prem, please include an example checklist of items the customer must provide (network CIDRs, bastion/jump hosts, firewall rules, and admin contacts). That will speed our procurement review.

If you can incorporate short, actionable answers to these three points in the final file that would be great. We'll route the final SIG to procurement and legal.

Best,
Jordan
---

On Mon, 14 Feb 2026 at 09:00, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Jordan — uploaded a final package to the Drive link and added the specific lines you asked for:
>
> - Hosted: enterprise customers can integrate with their KMS (customer-supplied keys) using our KMS connector; default is tenant-specific envelope keys; root/master key is not shared.
> - Dedicated: control plane performs orchestration but uses an agent for runtime actions; agent connections are mTLS and limited to orchestration commands; control plane cannot SSH into GPU hosts.
> - Private/on-prem: included checklist (network CIDRs, firewall ports, service account with least privilege, and point-of-contact).
>
> Final package: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/SIG/ACME/answers-v1 (attached archive contains the spreadsheet and diagrams).
>
> Karthik
